html.p: These chart types are ideal for hierarchical data and sequential stage analysis. Because they use nested data structures, the data is typically embedded directly in the option string rather than bound via seriesDataIndexBinding.

A treemap renders hierarchical data as nested rectangles. Area is proportional to value. Each node can have children to create sub-levels. This is useful for visualising cost breakdowns, log volume by source category, or file-system usage.
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

          <query>| makeresults</query>

    left: 'center'

  series: [

html.p: A sunburst chart arranges the same hierarchical data in concentric rings radiating outward from the root. Inner rings represent parent categories; outer rings represent leaf nodes. It is especially effective for showing proportional composition at each level simultaneously.

Key options: radius sets the inner/outer size, and label: { rotate: 'radial' } keeps labels readable at any angle. Clicking an inner ring drills down into that subtree; pressing Escape or clicking the centre navigates back up.

html.p: A funnel chart visualises a sequential process where values decrease at each stage. It is well suited to alert triage pipelines, sales conversion funnels, or any multi-step filtering workflow.
Set sort: 'descending' so the largest stage appears at the top. The gap property controls the spacing between stages in pixels.

pre.code: series: [{ name: 'Alert Triage', type: 'funnel', left: '10%', width: '80%', sort: 'descending', gap: 2, label: { show: true, position: 'inside' }, data: [ { value: 10000, name: 'Raw Events' }, { value: 5200, name: 'Correlated' }, { value: 1800, name: 'Notable Alerts' }, { value: 620, name: 'Investigated' }, { value: 180, name: 'Confirmed Incidents' }, { value: 45, name: 'Critical' } ] }]
